## Key finding on the console errors
When I probed the running services, **all three local services are currently UP and healthy** — so the 502/503s were a *service-availability snapshot*, not a code or database bug. Measured right now:

| `127.0.0.1:5001/api/zones` (Node direct) | **401** | Node up, route reachable, auth-gated (not 502) |

`netstat` confirms 5001, 8501, 5173 all `LISTENING`.

### 1. Exact reason for `/api/zones` 502
A **502 from the Vite proxy means the `/api` target `127.0.0.1:5001` (Node) was not reachable** at that moment — Node was not running, had exited after "FULLY READY", or was mid-restart. It is **not** a database error and **not** a bug in the zones route: `client/vite.config.js` correctly points `/api` → `127.0.0.1:5001`, and when Node is up the route returns 401/200, never 502. **No change made to the zones route** (the request must reach Node and Node must log a real exception before that's warranted — it doesn't).

### 2. Exact reason for YOLO 502 (`/api/yolo/people-count`, `/api/yolo/analyze-frame`)
The frontend ([ObjectDetection.jsx:12-13](client/src/pages/ObjectDetection.jsx#L12)) calls `/ai/api/yolo/...`. The Vite `/ai` proxy strips `/ai` and forwards to **Python `localhost:8501`**. A **502 means Python (uvicorn on 8501) was not running**. Frontend paths and the `/ai` proxy agree, and both endpoints exist in `ai-service/main.py` (`@app.get("/api/yolo/people-count")`, `@app.post("/api/yolo/analyze-frame")`). YOLO is **not** routed through Node — correct as-is. No change made.

### 3. Exact reason for facial track 503
`POST /api/facial-recognition/track` is a **Node** route ([facialRecognition.js:313](server/routes/facialRecognition.js#L313)) that forwards to **`http://127.0.0.1:8501/user/track`** using `FACE_AI_URL` (server/.env: `FACE_AI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8501` ✓), with header `X-AI-Service-Key`, a 5s timeout, and the Python endpoint confirmed present. When Python is down, Node catches `ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT` and **deliberately returns 503 "Face tracking service is offline"** — a correct fail-soft AI-offline signal. This is the healthy fallback and I left it intact. (Note: a 503 here while `/api/zones` shows 502 means Node was up but Python was down/starting — the two errors came from slightly different moments; if Node were fully down, track would also be 502.)

### 4. Exact reason for Pi stream timeout
`172.20.10.4:8081/video_feed` genuinely times out (still does now — curl exit 28). This is a **network/hardware reachability issue**, not a website/backend failure: the Pi is powered off, not on the same hotspot, or `172.20.10.4:8081` is a stale address/port. All changes are unstaged, nothing committed, branch and HEAD unchanged. Here is the final report. --- # User Management responsive rebuild — final report ## 1. Exact cause of the one-character mobile wrapping Two inherited-table behaviors combined: - **`.users-table { table-layout: fixed }` with percentage column widths** (`Personnel 20%`, `Email 21%`, `Status 9%`, etc.). When the previous CSS turned the table into a grid/flex card, those tiny percentage widths and the fixed-layout intrinsic sizing still pinned cells to a few `ch` of usable width at 390px. - **`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the name/email inside a zero-basis flex/grid item.** Unlike `break-word`, `anywhere` *lowers the element's min-content size to a single character*, so a flex/grid item with no reserved `min-width`/`flex-basis` collapses to ~1ch and the text wraps one letter per line. That is the exact mechanism behind the vertical `J\na\nn\ne` name and the unreadable vertical email. ## 2. Why the previous table-to-card CSS approach failed Re-`display`-ing `//
` does not fully shed table sizing: `table-layout: fixed`, percentage `width`, and min-content interactions keep leaking into the "cards," so widths resolve wrong at narrow viewports. Layering `td::before` labels + `order` + `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on top of that made it fragile and order-dependent — cards read as broken table rows (tall, sparse at 1024px; collapsed columns at 390px). A table row is simply not a robust card primitive. ## 3. JSX structure added ([Users.jsx](client/src/pages/Users.jsx)) Kept the desktop `` and added a **separate, purpose-built card DOM** rendered from the *same* `filteredUsers`. Shared logic was extracted so nothing is duplicated: `renderRoleBadge`, `renderStatusBadge`, `renderFaceIdTag`, `formatJoined`, and `renderUserActions(u, isSelf)` are used by **both** representations (one data fetch, one set of handlers). ``` {loading ? : empty ? : ( …
// >=1025px // <=1024px avatar · name(+You) · [role badge+desc] · [status] Email (full-width) · Face ID · Joined View Logs · Suspend/Reactivate · Delete ``` No fields removed, no actions removed, FM-only `+ Add Tenant` and self-row disabling untouched. ## 4. Breakpoint behaviour ([Users.css](client/src/css/Users.css)) - **≥1367px** desktop table; **1025–1366px** existing laptop table tuning; **`.user-card-list { display:none }`**. - **≤1024px** `.users-desktop-table { display:none }`, card list becomes a `grid`. Pure **CSS display toggle** — only one representation is ever visible; both live in the DOM. - **≤640px** phone layout. ## 5. Phone card layout (≤640px) - Header: avatar + name + role badge(+description) + status badge (wraps). - Metadata: **single-column** `dt/dd` rows (Email, Face ID, Joined); label above value. - Name uses `overflow-wrap: break-word; word-break: normal` (wraps on spaces, **never per-character**); only `.email-value` uses `overflow-wrap: anywhere` — and it sits in a full-width grid cell with `min-width:0`, so it wraps as a readable block, not a column. - Actions: 2-col grid (**View Logs | Suspend/Reactivate**) with **Delete spanning the full row below**; `min-height: 44px`; Delete keeps its destructive red styling. - `.user-card { width:100%; min-width:0; box-sizing:border-box }`. ## 6. Tablet card layout (641–1024px) - Same header. - Metadata: `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.5fr) minmax(140px, 1fr)`; **Email spans both columns**, Face ID + Joined sit side by side — compact, no huge blank areas. - Actions: **single equal-height row** of three buttons (`repeat(3, 1fr)`, `min-height:44px`). - Summary grid → 2 columns; search full width with the three selects on the row below. ## 7. Results at 390 / 430 / 711 / 768 / 1024px I must be transparent: **I could not capture real authenticated screenshots.** The in-app Browser pane blocks all local origins (`localhost:5173`, `127.0.0.1`, and `file://` are refused "by policy"), a local static server was likewise blocked, and `list_connected_browsers` for your real Chrome returned `[]` — no surface in this environment can reach the logged-in page. So the pixel pass at those widths remains yours to run. What the CSS now guarantees structurally (and what tests lock): 390/430 → single-column labelled cards, names wrap on words, email wraps as a block, 2-col actions + full-width Delete, ~44px targets; 711/768 → full-width cards, two-column metadata, one action row; 1024 → compact tablet cards (not the old sparse ones). The one-character wrap is now **structurally impossible** because values render in block/grid cells with `min-width:0` and `word-break:normal`, and no table sizing is inherited. ## 8. Horizontal overflow None expected: cards are `width:100%; min-width:0; box-sizing:border-box`, only the email may break inside a token, and the page keeps the safe-area bottom padding from the earlier pass so the chatbot FAB / reCAPTCHA don't cover the last card's actions (Part 6).
